title: Get started
text: Build plot usual add theme_bauhaus(). default dial Turquoise, screensaver’s default.  Pick another dial name. Case, spaces underscores don’t matter, "Signal Blue", "signal-blue" "signal_blue" dial.  dial also shortcut: theme_bauhaus_ocean(), theme_bauhaus_signal_blue() .
code: penguins <- na.omit(palmerpenguins::penguins)  p <- ggplot(penguins, aes(flipper_length_mm, body_mass_g, colour = species)) +   geom_point(size = 1.8, alpha = 0.9) +   labs(     title = "Palmer penguins",     subtitle = "Body mass against flipper length",     x = "Flipper length (mm)", y = "Body mass (g)", colour = "Species",     caption = "Data: palmerpenguins"   )  p + theme_bauhaus() bauhaus_dial_names(display = TRUE) #>  [1] "White"       "Turquoise"   "Glacier"     "Ocean"       "Tennis"      #>  [6] "Signal Blue" "Salmon"      "Yellow"      "Beige"       "Pistachio"   #> [11] "Lavender"    "Rose"        "Sky Blue"    "Cream"       "Slate"       #> [16] "Noir" p + theme_bauhaus("ocean") p + theme_bauhaus_yellow()

title: Get started
text: Bauhaus theme complete ggplot2 theme. sets: theme alone gives matching colours. chart discrete continuous fills:   Single-colour geoms use numeral ink, smoothers use accent:
code: bars <- ggplot(mpg, aes(class, fill = drv)) +   geom_bar() +   coord_flip() +   labs(title = "Cars by class", x = NULL, y = "Count", fill = "Drive")  bars + theme_bauhaus("salmon", grid = "x") ggplot(faithfuld, aes(waiting, eruptions, fill = density)) +   geom_raster() +   coord_cartesian(expand = FALSE) +   labs(title = "Old Faithful", x = "Waiting time (min)", y = "Eruption (min)", fill = "Density") +   theme_bauhaus("glacier") ggplot(economics, aes(date, unemploy / 1000)) +   geom_line(linewidth = 0.5) +   geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, span = 0.3) +   labs(title = "US unemployment", x = NULL, y = "Unemployed (millions)") +   theme_bauhaus("rose")

title: Get started
text: theme_bauhaus() takes usual base_size, base_family header_family, plus : grid: major grid lines draw, "xy" (default), "x", "y" "none". grain: TRUE dial’s measured grain, FALSE flat plate, number set strength (standard deviation 8-bit code values). grain_density: grain samples per inch. default, 150, matches screensaver Retina laptop screen; lower coarser grain.  use dial every plot session, set :
code: p + theme_bauhaus("beige", base_size = 12, grid = "y", grain = 9, grain_density = 90) theme_set(theme_bauhaus("pistachio"))

title: Get started
text: theme already sets dial’s palettes defaults. Add scale want another dial’s palette, reversed one, scale arguments.  palettes also available plain colour vectors palette functions, base graphics packages: See palettes article every dial’s colours.
code: ggplot(mpg, aes(displ, hwy, colour = cty)) +   geom_point(size = 2) +   scale_colour_bauhaus_b("tennis", n.breaks = 6) +   labs(title = "Binned colour scale", x = "Displacement (l)", y = "Highway mpg", colour = "City mpg") +   theme_bauhaus("tennis") bauhaus_palette("turquoise") #> [1] "#007C84" "#D31C3F" "#9B7C00" "#004F5D" "#5D6195" "#00753E" "#970000" #> [8] "#152D55" bauhaus_palette("turquoise", type = "sequential", n = 5) #> [1] "#E4FEFF" "#84BBC0" "#007C84" "#006570" "#004F5D" pal_bauhaus("noir")(3) #> [1] "#E0E0DC" "#FFC800" "#00AFEC"

title: Get started
text: bauhaus_colours() returns everything measured dial, handy annotations:
code: col <- bauhaus_colours("lavender") col #>          paper          plate        numeral          track          steel  #>      "#CFD6F5"      "#C2C9E8"      "#364379"      "#6570A6"      "#E2E3E8"  #>           hand           lume      lume_hand            hub    shadow_core  #>      "#DFE1E7"      "#EEFCFC"      "#E9F6F5"      "#D2D4DA"      "#5D6195"  #> shadow_ambient shadow_contact  #>      "#787EB4"      "#2B366C" ggplot(economics, aes(date, psavert)) +   annotate("rect",     xmin = as.Date("2007-12-01"), xmax = as.Date("2009-06-01"), ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,     fill = col[["shadow_ambient"]], alpha = 0.25   ) +   geom_line() +   annotate("text",     x = as.Date("2007-09-01"), y = 15, label = "Great Recession", hjust = 1,     colour = col[["track"]], family = bauhaus_font_family(), size = 3.5   ) +   labs(title = "Personal saving rate", x = NULL, y = "% of disposable income") +   theme_bauhaus("lavender")

title: Get started
text: package bundles Zalando Sans Expanded (SIL Open Font License) registers systemfonts loads, nothing needs installing. Devices built systemfonts find automatically: ragg: ggsave() uses PNG, JPEG TIFF whenever ragg installed. R Markdown Quarto, set chunk option dev = "ragg_png". RStudio, choose Tools › Global Options › General › Graphics › Backend: AGG. Positron uses ragg installed. svglite SVG. devices don’t know bundled font. pdf(), postscript() default macOS screen device (Quartz) fall back Helvetica, default Windows screen device system sans. get real typeface , render text showtext: use Cairo PDF device, ggsave("plot.pdf", device = cairo_pdf), installing font files bauhaus_font_files() system.
code: bauhaus_showtext() # registers the fonts with showtext and turns it on pdf("plot.pdf", width = 7, height = 4.5) print(p + theme_bauhaus()) dev.off()

title: Get started
text: ggsave() takes background colour theme. grain drawn raster image, works every device makes PDF SVG files larger. vector output can switch whole session:
code: ggsave("penguins.png", p + theme_bauhaus("ocean"), width = 7, height = 4.5, dpi = 300) options(bauhaus.grain = FALSE)

title: Get started
text: plot draws grained background. combine plots patchwork, give whole layout theme , space around plots paper well:
code: library(patchwork)  a <- ggplot(penguins, aes(bill_length_mm, bill_depth_mm, colour = species)) +   geom_point(show.legend = FALSE) +   labs(x = "Bill length (mm)", y = "Bill depth (mm)") b <- ggplot(penguins, aes(species, fill = species)) +   geom_bar(show.legend = FALSE) +   labs(x = NULL, y = "Count")  (a | b) +   plot_annotation(title = "Penguins", theme = theme_bauhaus("sky_blue")) &   theme_bauhaus("sky_blue")

title: Drawing the dial
text: Everything dial, numerals included, drawn shapes, scales size. Save square:
code: ggsave("noir.png", bauhaus_clock("noir"), width = 4, height = 4, dpi = 300)

title: Drawing the dial
text: default time, 10:08:13, one shown screensaver’s reference renders. Pass time "HH:MM", "HH:MM:SS" date-time, example Sys.time():
code: library(patchwork)  bauhaus_clock("salmon", time = "16:42:30") |   bauhaus_clock("glacier", time = "07:15", seconds = FALSE)

title: Drawing the dial
text: Leave seconds hand minute numerals quieter face, grain flat plate:
code: bauhaus_clock("lavender", time = "12:52", seconds = FALSE, minute_numerals = FALSE)

title: Drawing the dial
code: clocks <- lapply(bauhaus_dial_names(), bauhaus_clock, minute_numerals = FALSE) wrap_plots(clocks, ncol = 4) &   theme(plot.margin = margin(2, 2, 2, 2))

title: Drawing the dial
text: result ordinary ggplot, can add . plot runs -1.16 1.16 axes (-1.04 without minute numerals), end 12 o’clock index y = 1.
code: col <- bauhaus_colours("pistachio") bauhaus_clock("pistachio", time = "09:00", seconds = FALSE) +   annotate("text",     x = 0, y = -0.33, label = "ggplot2", colour = col[["track"]],     family = bauhaus_font_family("semibold")   )

knitr::opts_chunk$set( echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, dev = "ragg_png", fig.width = 9, fig.height = 4, out.width = "100%" ) library(ggplot2) library(bauhaus) library(patchwork) penguins <- na.omit(palmerpenguins::penguins) # The dial on the left, a chart on the right, on one sheet of the dial's paper. Extra theme # settings for the chart go in `...`. showcase <- function(dial, chart, grid = "xy", ...) { clock <- bauhaus_clock(dial) chart <- chart + theme_bauhaus(dial, base_size = 10.5, grid = grid) + theme(...) (clock | chart) + plot_layout(widths = c(1, 1.45)) + plot_annotation(theme = theme_bauhaus(dial) + theme(plot.margin = margin(14, 14, 14, 14))) } dial_note <- function(dial) { d <- bauhaus_dials[bauhaus_dials$dial == dial, ] grain <- if (d$grain == 0) "no grain" else sprintf("grain σ %.2g", d$grain) cat(sprintf( "

theme_bauhaus(\"%s\") · paper %s · numerals %s · track %s · %s

\n", dial, d$paper, d$numeral, d$track, grain )) } white <- ggplot(penguins, aes(bill_length_mm, bill_depth_mm, colour = species)) + geom_point(size = 1.4, alpha = 0.85) + geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE, linewidth = 0.7) + labs( title = "Bill shape by species", subtitle = "Palmer penguins", x = "Bill length (mm)", y = "Bill depth (mm)", colour = NULL ) showcase("white", white) by_count <- function(x) factor(x, levels = names(sort(table(x)))) turquoise <- ggplot(mpg, aes(y = by_count(class), fill = drv)) + geom_bar(width = 0.75) + labs(title = "Cars by class", subtitle = "Stacked by drive train", x = "Count", y = NULL, fill = "Drive") showcase("turquoise", turquoise, grid = "x") glacier <- ggplot(faithfuld, aes(waiting, eruptions, fill = density)) + geom_raster(interpolate = TRUE) + coord_cartesian(expand = FALSE) + labs( title = "Old Faithful", subtitle = "Density of eruptions", x = "Waiting time (min)", y = "Eruption (min)", fill = NULL ) showcase("glacier", glacier) econ <- subset(economics_long, variable %in% c("psavert", "uempmed", "unemploy")) econ$variable <- factor(econ$variable, levels = c("unemploy", "uempmed", "psavert"), labels = c("Unemployed", "Weeks unemployed", "Saving rate") ) ocean <- ggplot(econ, aes(date, value01, colour = variable)) + geom_line(linewidth = 0.55) + labs( title = "The US economy", subtitle = "Each series scaled to 0-1", x = NULL, y = NULL, colour = NULL ) showcase("ocean", ocean, legend.position = "top") tennis <- ggplot(diamonds, aes(carat, fill = cut)) + geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.1, boundary = 0) + coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 3)) + labs(title = "Diamonds", subtitle = "Carat, stacked by cut", x = "Carat", y = "Count", fill = NULL) showcase("tennis", tennis) cars <- mtcars[order(mtcars$mpg), ] cars$model <- factor(rownames(cars), levels = rownames(cars)) cars <- tail(cars, 14) signal_blue <- ggplot(cars, aes(mpg, model)) + geom_segment(aes(x = 10, xend = mpg, yend = model), linewidth = 0.4, colour = "#9FFFFF") + geom_point(size = 2.4) + labs(title = "Most frugal cars", subtitle = "Motor Trend, 1974", x = "Miles per gallon", y = NULL) showcase("signal_blue", signal_blue, grid = "x") salmon <- ggplot(penguins, aes(body_mass_g, fill = species, colour = species)) + geom_density(alpha = 0.35, linewidth = 0.6) + labs(title = "Body mass", subtitle = "Palmer penguins", x = "Body mass (g)", y = NULL, fill = NULL, colour = NULL) showcase("salmon", salmon) cities <- subset(txhousing, city %in% c("Austin", "Dallas", "Houston", "San Antonio")) yellow <- ggplot(cities, aes(date, median / 1000, colour = city)) + geom_line(linewidth = 0.5) + labs(title = "Texas house prices", subtitle = "Monthly median sale price", x = NULL, y = "$ thousands", colour = NULL) showcase("yellow", yellow) beige <- ggplot(mpg, aes(reorder(class, hwy, median), hwy)) + geom_boxplot(width = 0.6, outlier.size = 0.9) + labs(title = "Highway mileage", subtitle = "By class of car", x = NULL, y = "Miles per gallon") showcase("beige", beige, grid = "y") pistachio <- ggplot(penguins, aes(flipper_length_mm, body_mass_g / 1000, colour = sex)) + geom_point(size = 1, alpha = 0.85) + facet_wrap(~island) + labs(title = "Penguins by island", x = "Flipper (mm)", y = "Mass (kg)", colour = NULL) showcase("pistachio", pistachio, legend.position = "top") r <- abs(cor(mtcars[, c("mpg", "disp", "hp", "drat", "wt", "qsec")])) cors <- data.frame(x = rep(colnames(r), each = nrow(r)), y = rep(rownames(r), ncol(r)), r = as.vector(r)) lavender <- ggplot(cors, aes(x, y, fill = r)) + geom_tile(colour = bauhaus_colours("lavender")[["paper"]], linewidth = 1) + geom_text( aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", r), colour = I(ifelse(r > 0.55, "white", bauhaus_colours("lavender")[["numeral"]]))), size = 2.6, family = bauhaus_font_family() ) + coord_fixed() + labs(title = "Correlations", subtitle = "Absolute values, mtcars", x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "|r|") showcase("lavender", lavender, grid = "none") rose <- ggplot(subset(economics, date > as.Date("1990-01-01")), aes(date, psavert)) + geom_area(alpha = 0.3, fill = bauhaus_colours("rose")[["track"]]) + geom_line(linewidth = 0.6) + labs(title = "Personal saving rate", subtitle = "United States", x = NULL, y = "% of income") showcase("rose", rose) sky_blue <- ggplot(midwest, aes(percollege, percbelowpoverty, size = poptotal, colour = state)) + geom_point(alpha = 0.6) + scale_size_area(max_size = 7, guide = "none") + scale_x_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) + scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) + labs(title = "Midwest counties", subtitle = "Education and poverty", x = "College educated", y = "Below poverty", colour = NULL) showcase("sky_blue", sky_blue) set.seed(1) dsample <- diamonds[sample(nrow(diamonds), 1500), ] cream <- ggplot(dsample, aes(cut, price / 1000, colour = cut)) + geom_violin(fill = NA, linewidth = 0.5, show.legend = FALSE) + geom_jitter(width = 0.15, size = 0.5, alpha = 0.5, show.legend = FALSE) + labs(title = "Diamond prices", subtitle = "A sample of 1,500 stones", x = NULL, y = "$ thousands") showcase("cream", cream, grid = "y") yearly <- aggregate(sales ~ year + city, data = subset(txhousing, city %in% c("Austin", "Dallas", "Houston", "Fort Worth", "San Antonio")), FUN = sum) slate <- ggplot(yearly, aes(year, sales / 1000, colour = city)) + geom_line(linewidth = 0.6) + geom_point(size = 1.1) + labs(title = "Texas home sales", subtitle = "Homes sold per year", x = NULL, y = "Thousands", colour = NULL) showcase("slate", slate) noir <- ggplot(faithful, aes(waiting, eruptions)) + stat_density_2d(geom = "polygon", aes(fill = after_stat(level)), bins = 9) + geom_point(size = 0.6, alpha = 0.7) + labs(title = "Old Faithful", subtitle = "Contours of the joint density", x = "Waiting time (min)", y = "Eruption (min)", fill = NULL) showcase("noir", noir)

text: grain screensaver’s , generated way seed: Uniform white noise 32-bit xorshift generator fills seamless 512 x 512 tile. noise passed small 7 x 5 kernel measured original artwork. kernel smooths along rows sharpens across , grain made short horizontal streaks, two three samples long. mottling, gradient, vignette fibre. result scaled unit variance tails softened. dial, plate colour lifted 13/255 grain added equally red, green blue, strength measured dial. strengths, standard deviations 8-bit code values: close, grain Tennis dial looks like (magnified eight times):

title: The paper grain
text: Every Bauhaus theme puts grain plot background, using element_grain(). Panels, legends strips left transparent, grain runs whole plot, runs whole screen screensaver. grain drawn fixed physical size, 150 samples per inch default, looks small figure poster. density matches screensaver Retina laptop screen.
code: p <- ggplot(mpg, aes(displ, hwy)) +   geom_point(size = 2) +   labs(title = "Default grain", x = "Displacement (l)", y = "Highway mpg")  p + theme_bauhaus("tennis")

text: grain sets strength grain_density size:
code: p + labs(title = "grain = 12, grain_density = 70") +   theme_bauhaus("tennis", grain = 12, grain_density = 70) p + labs(title = "grain = FALSE") +   theme_bauhaus("tennis", grain = FALSE)

title: The paper grain
text: element_grain() rectangle element like element_rect(), can go anywhere rectangle can, theme:   Adding plain element_rect() top keeps grain unless sets fill, can add border without losing paper:
code: ggplot(mpg, aes(class)) +   geom_bar(fill = "#30475E") +   labs(title = "theme_classic() on grained paper", x = NULL, y = "Count") +   theme_classic(base_family = bauhaus_font_family()) +   theme(plot.background = element_grain(fill = "#F2EBDD", sigma = 6, colour = NA)) ggplot(mpg, aes(displ, hwy)) +   geom_point(colour = "white") +   labs(title = "Grain on the panel only", x = "Displacement (l)", y = "Highway mpg") +   theme_bauhaus("white") +   theme(panel.background = element_grain(fill = bauhaus_colours("ocean")[["paper"]], sigma = 5.3, colour = NA)) p + labs(title = "A border on the grained background") +   theme_bauhaus("salmon") +   theme(plot.background = element_rect(colour = bauhaus_colours("salmon")[["track"]], linewidth = 1.5))

title: Colours and palettes
text: dial screensaver small colour system. colours measured dial artwork stored bauhaus_dials: paper plate: plate shown screen (lifted 13/255) nominal colour. numeral: hour numerals. track: minute track minute numerals. steel, hand hub: polished steel indices, hands hub. lume lume_hand: luminous paint indices hands, daylight. shadow_core, shadow_ambient shadow_contact: tinted shadows hands indices. coloured dials deep, saturated versions plate. palettes built : discrete palette eight colours. opens dial’s signature colour ink, borrows accents dials (plates, inks shadow tints), chosen stand dial’s plate. Apart dial’s inks two mid-tone plates, Signal Blue Tennis, first six colours every palette reach contrast ratio least 3:1 paper. sequential palette ramp dial’s colours. light dials runs daylight lume signature colour numeral ink; dark dials rises just plate track ink numeral ink.

text: Inside Bauhaus theme dial’s palettes already defaults. Scales let use another dial’s palette, reverse , bin :   work themes well:  discrete palettes stop eight colours, categories hard tell apart. groups, ggplot2 warns leaves extra ones grey; consider lumping smallest groups together. base graphics, use colour vectors directly:
code: ggplot(faithfuld, aes(waiting, eruptions, fill = density)) +   geom_raster() +   scale_fill_bauhaus_c("sky_blue", reverse = TRUE) +   coord_cartesian(expand = FALSE) +   labs(title = "Reversed sequential palette", x = "Waiting (min)", y = "Eruption (min)") +   theme_bauhaus("sky_blue") ggplot(faithfuld, aes(waiting, eruptions, z = density)) +   geom_contour_filled(bins = 7) +   scale_fill_bauhaus_d("salmon") +   coord_cartesian(expand = FALSE) +   labs(title = "Filled contours", x = "Waiting (min)", y = "Eruption (min)", fill = "Density") +   theme_bauhaus("cream") ggplot(mpg, aes(displ, hwy, colour = class)) +   geom_point(size = 2) +   scale_colour_bauhaus_d("turquoise") +   labs(title = "A Bauhaus palette on theme_minimal()", x = "Displacement (l)", y = "Highway mpg") +   theme_minimal() op <- par(bg = bauhaus_colours("yellow")[["paper"]], family = "sans") barplot(VADeaths, beside = TRUE, col = bauhaus_palette("yellow", n = 5), border = NA) par(op)

title: bauhaus: ggplot2 themes from the Bauhaus Clock dials
text: ggplot2 themes dials Bauhaus Clock screensaver. bauhaus brings sixteen day dials Bauhaus Clock macOS screensaver ggplot2. Every theme paints plot dial’s paper plate, complete screensaver’s fine paper grain, sets type screensaver’s typeface, takes text, grid, geom palette colours inks, steel, lume shadow tints measured dial.  sixteen dials, drawn bauhaus_clock(). Sixteen themes: White, Turquoise, Glacier, Ocean, Tennis, Signal Blue, Salmon, Yellow, Beige, Pistachio, Lavender, Rose, Sky Blue, Cream, Slate Noir. day dials included. screensaver’s paper grain, generated algorithm, kernel seed, strength measured dial. screensaver’s typeface, Zalando Sans Expanded, bundled registered automatically. Matching palettes scales: eight-colour discrete palette sequential ramp per dial, set plot’s defaults theme. dial : bauhaus_clock() draws clock face, time, colourway. See website gallery every dial full documentation.

title: bauhaus: ggplot2 themes from the Bauhaus Clock dials
text: theme_bauhaus() returns complete theme, replaces whatever theme plot . sets: Background: dial’s paper grain, whole plot (panels, legends strips transparent). Type: Zalando Sans Expanded body text semibold weight titles. Ink: titles, axis titles default geom colour use hour-numeral ink; subtitles, captions, axis labels, ticks grid lines use minute-track ink, round line ends like track’s ticks. track ink faint read (Cream Slate), pushed towards numeral ink. Palettes: dial’s discrete palette discrete colour fill, sequential palette continuous colour fill, accent things like geom_smooth(). single theme call gives matching colours throughout:  Options: Set dial every plot session theme_set(theme_bauhaus("pistachio")).
code: bars <- ggplot(mpg, aes(y = class, fill = drv)) +   geom_bar() +   labs(title = "Cars by class", x = "Count", y = NULL, fill = "Drive") +   theme_bauhaus("salmon", grid = "x")  heat <- ggplot(faithfuld, aes(waiting, eruptions, fill = density)) +   geom_raster() +   coord_cartesian(expand = FALSE) +   labs(title = "Old Faithful", x = "Waiting (min)", y = "Eruption (min)", fill = NULL) +   theme_bauhaus("salmon")  (bars | heat) + plot_annotation(theme = theme_bauhaus("salmon"))

text: bauhaus_showtext() registers bundled fonts showtext turns showtext , every device draws real typeface: pdf(), default Quartz Windows screen devices, RStudio’s default backend. needs showtext package: Call per R session, drawing: things know: saving PNG, JPEG TIFF showtext , tell showtext resolution text comes right size: showtext::showtext_opts(dpi = 300) ggsave("plot.png", dpi = 300). bauhaus_showtext(enable = FALSE) registers fonts without turning showtext everything. title: Bauhaus Clock themes — theme_bauhaus
code: theme_bauhaus(   dial = "turquoise",   base_size = 11,   base_family = bauhaus_font_family(),   header_family = bauhaus_font_family("semibold"),   base_line_size = base_size/22,   base_rect_size = base_size/22,   grain = TRUE,   grain_density = 150,   grid = c("xy", "x", "y", "none") )

title: Bauhaus Clock themes — theme_bauhaus
text: dial dial name. Case, spaces, hyphens underscores ignored, "Signal Blue", "signal-blue" "signal_blue" work. See bauhaus_dial_names(). base_size Base font size, points. base_family Font family body text. header_family Font family titles. base_line_size Base size line elements. base_rect_size Base size rect elements. grain Paper grain. TRUE uses grain strength measured dial, FALSE draws flat plate, number sets strength (standard deviation 8-bit code values). grain_density Grain samples per inch. Lower values give coarser grain. grid major grid lines draw: "xy", "x", "y" "none".

text: complete ggplot2 theme.

title: Bauhaus Clock themes — theme_bauhaus
text: Background: dial's plate, lifted screensaver lifts , screensaver's paper grain strength measured dial (see element_grain()). Type: Zalando Sans Expanded, screensaver's typeface (see bauhaus_font_family()). Titles use semibold weight. Colour: titles default geom colour use hour-numeral ink; axis labels, ticks grid lines use minute-track ink, round line ends like track's ticks. Palettes: dial's discrete sequential palettes become plot's default colour fill scales (see bauhaus_palette()), accent colour used things like ggplot2::geom_smooth(). dial also shortcut, theme_bauhaus_turquoise().

title: Bauhaus Clock themes — theme_bauhaus
text: bundled fonts registered systemfonts, ragg svglite devices use. ggplot2::ggsave() uses ragg PNG, JPEG TIFF files installed. R Markdown Quarto, set chunk option dev = "ragg_png"; RStudio, choose "AGG" graphics backend. devices call bauhaus_showtext() first, pass base_family = "sans".

title: Bauhaus Clock themes — theme_bauhaus
code: library(ggplot2)  p <- ggplot(mpg, aes(displ, hwy, colour = drv)) +   geom_point(size = 2) +   labs(     title = "Fuel economy",     subtitle = "Highway miles per gallon by engine size",     x = "Displacement (litres)", y = "Highway mpg", colour = "Drive"   )  p + theme_bauhaus()  p + theme_bauhaus("ocean")  p + theme_bauhaus_yellow(grid = "y")

title: bauhaus 0.1.0
text: First release. theme_bauhaus() one shortcut per dial: sixteen ggplot2 themes day dials Bauhaus Clock screensaver, screensaver’s paper grain, typeface measured colours. element_grain(), paper grain theme element works theme. Discrete, continuous binned colour scales (scale_colour_bauhaus_d() friends) palettes behind (bauhaus_palette(), pal_bauhaus(), pal_bauhaus_c()). bauhaus_colours() bauhaus_dials, measured colours every dial. Zalando Sans Expanded bundled registered systemfonts load; bauhaus_showtext() covers devices don’t use systemfonts. bauhaus_clock() draws dial .
